dct_description_sm: The purpose of this project is to quantify sea ice dynamics in the Beaufort Sea region using a state of the art ice tracking algorithm from Environment Canada applied to the archive of RADARSAT image data.  Oil and gas exploration in the region requires detailed knowledge of sea ice dynamics due to the potential damage by sea ice to platforms and other infrastructure. While it is widely known that sea ice within the Beaufort Sea region circulates according to the Beaufort Gyre, very little quantitative information about sea ice motion exists. Buoy data from the International Arctic Buoy Programme over the Beaufort Sea region is sparse and not available at sufficiently high spatial resolution to resolve local scale motion characteristics. High resolution (100-200 m) satellite imagery from RADARSAT has shown utility for estimating sea ice motion. Sea ice motion information will specifically be provided to collaborators in the Meteorological Research Division of Environment Canada who require satellite-derived ice motion information for the evaluation and tuning of a new regional sea ice forecasting system for the Beaufort Sea. The data will also be available publicly once the data collection and analysis process is complete.
dct_title_s: Quantifying Sea Ice Dynamics in the Beaufort Sea
